claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child I'm responsible for - just the one. Their name is Alex, they're 15 years old and live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

Now, to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask: do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's helpful to know.

Just to confirm - are you the person responsible for Alex's day-to-day care? By this I mean, do you provide for their needs such as food, clothes, accommodation, and other living expenses?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex's day-to-day care - I provide for all their needs like food, clothes, a place to live, all the usual things a parent does.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? (Remember, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually a bit of a situation. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for them, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. So no one is claiming it right now, but we're both involved in Alex's care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that situation. I understand you and Alex's other parent are both involved in their care but haven't agreed on who should claim.

To help me understand the living arrangements better: does Alex live with you full-time, or does Alex split their time between you and the other parent (for example, spending some days/weeks with each of you)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me full-time - they're at home with me all the time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex lives with you full-time.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment. You mentioned Alex is 15 years old. Can you tell me:

1. Is Alex currently in education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is still in school - they're doing their GCSEs at the moment, just normal secondary school stuff for their age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

Just one final question to ensure I have a complete picture: Are there any other circumstances that might affect Alex's situation, such as:

- Is Alex in hospital or residential care for an extended period?
- Has Alex started working 24 hours or more per week?
- Is Alex claiming any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. Alex isn't in hospital or any kind of residential care, they're not working at all - just focused on school - and they're not claiming any benefits themselves. Just a normal 15-year-old really, living at home and studying.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 15 years old and living with you full-time in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and provide for all their needs
- Alex is in approved education (secondary school, doing GCSEs)
- Alex is not in hospital, care, working 24+ hours, or claiming benefits
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You meet all the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. Regarding the disagreement with Alex's other parent about who should claim - since Alex lives with you full-time and you're providing their day-to-day care, you would be the appropriate person to claim. The rules state that only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. If you and the other parent cannot agree, HMRC can make the decision, but in cases where the child lives full-time with one parent who provides all their care, that parent would typically be the one to receive it.

You are eligible to apply for Child Benefit for Alex.
